key_insight: All-to-all self-attention is not strictly necessary for strong visual representations; adaptively constrained, learnable attention 'cores' can preserve representation quality while drastically lowering compute cost for high-resolution images.
problem_solved: Reduces the quadratic compute and memory bottleneck of Vision Transformers at high image resolutions, enabling scalable ViTs for dense, high-res visual tasks.
method: Introduce Elastic Attention Cores: learnable, flexible attention regions that allocate attention budget adaptively across tokens and scales instead of full pairwise attention.
Structured sparse/multi-scale attention: combine local core-centric attention with selective long-range aggregation to approximate global interactions with much lower complexity.
Plug-and-play design: integrate cores into standard ViT blocks so models retain training regimes and transferability while reducing runtime and memory.
impact: Makes ViTs practical for high-resolution vision tasks (e.g., remote sensing, medical imaging, dense prediction) by cutting compute and memory needs, enabling larger inputs or faster inference without sacrificing representational power.
visual_elements: Complexity diagram: quadratic all-to-all attention vs. near-linear elastic-core attention (compute/memory vs. resolution curve).
Architecture schematic: ViT block showing where Elastic Attention Cores plug in (local cores + selective global links).
Attention map heatmaps: example original full attention vs. sparse elastic-core attention to show focused interactions.
Performance vs. resolution bar/line chart: accuracy/throughput trade-off illustrating preserved accuracy with lower compute at increasing resolutions.
paper_title: Elastic Attention Cores for Scalable Vision Transformers
paper_authors: Alan Z. Song, Yinjie Chen, Mu Nan, Rui Zhang, Jiahang Cao
